title: Global Critical Minerals Outlook 2026: Executive summary
key_claim: Recycling capacity is more concentrated than mining, with China holding over three-quarters of global battery pre-treatment capacity and 90% of material recovery capacity, while benchmark copper smelter fees settled at USD 0 per tonne in 2026, the lowest ever agreed.
frame_summary: The IEA is arguing that secondary supply is not an escape from concentration risk, because the processing capacity that turns scrap into usable metal is itself concentrated and financially failing outside China.
verbatim_quote: Battery recycling capacity has expanded significantly, but remains highly concentrated, with China accounting for over three-quarters of global pre-treatment capacity and 90% of material recovery capacity.
verbatim_list: Benchmark copper smelter fees were settled at USD 0 per tonne in 2026, the lowest level ever agreed in annual negotiations, while spot charges have remained negative since 2024; zinc and lead smelter fees have also turned negative.
notes: Anchors the counter-intuitive point that retaining scrap does not by itself create the capacity to process it.

publisher: Presidence de la Republique (Elysee), G7 Evian 2026
title: G7 Leaders' Declaration on Securing Supply Chains for Critical Minerals
key_claim: G7 leaders committed to increasing collection and recycling capacity to avoid the leakage of valuable and end-of-life products containing critical raw materials, and to work towards recycling targets for selected critical minerals by the end of 2026.
frame_summary: The G7 is arguing that end-of-life material rich in critical minerals is a security asset that should be retained inside the bloc and traded only with trusted partners.
verbatim_quote: We seek to increase and enhance the collection and recycling capacity of the G7 to avoid the leakage of valuable and end-of-life products containing critical raw materials and to better combat the illegal transfer of waste rich in critical minerals by improving its traceability and enforcement of relevant laws and international frameworks.
verbatim_list: We will work towards recycling targets by the end of the year for selected critical minerals or their derivatives.
notes: First G7-level codification of scrap retention. Original-language French text confirmed at the Elysee's parallel URL.

title: Secondary aluminum outlook: the implications of proposed EU aluminum scrap export restrictions
key_claim: High-grade auto shredded scrap prices rose 42.2% between 2 January and 11 June 2026 and 226-grade alloy prices rose 42.7%, while EU aluminium scrap exports rose 74.7% year on year in March 2026 alone.
frame_summary: S&P Global is arguing that the retention debate has become urgent because European scrap is being bid away by external buyers at record prices, not because of a slow policy timetable.
verbatim_quote: High-grade auto shredded scrap prices, known as Twitch, jumped 42.2% from €1,800/metric ton DDP Germany on January 2 to €2,560/mt on June 11, while 226-grade alloy prices climbed 42.7% from €2,330/mt to a peak of €3,325/mt DDP Germany on June 12.
verbatim_list: In March 2026 alone, aluminum scrap exports from the EU rose 74.7% year over year, data from S&P Global Market Intelligence's Global Trade Atlas Analytics Suite showed.
notes: Supplies the price and volume anchors that make the policy move legible as a response to a market squeeze.

title: EU's Al scrap export measure unlikely in 2026
key_claim: The European Commission is expected to propose a 15% tariff on aluminium scrap exports on 9 September 2026, but a further consultation will follow, probably pushing implementation of any tariff into 2027 even if member states agree.
frame_summary: Argus is arguing that the retention measure remains an intention on a slipping timetable rather than an instrument in force, and that the market should price the delay.
verbatim_quote: But the EU now looks set to make an official proposal to impose a 15pc tariff on aluminium scrap exports on 9 September, sources confirmed to *Argus*. A further consultation process will surely follow such a proposal, probably pushing the implementation of any tariff into next year even if EU member states agree to it.
notes: Primary counter-evidence on timing. Quote reproduced with the page's inline emphasis markers as rendered.

title: Mercedes-Hydro deal points to growing pull for post-consumer aluminium scrap
key_claim: Carmakers are contracting for batch-verified post-consumer scrap, with Hydro CIRCAL made from at least 75% post-consumer scrap tracked and documented per batch under DNV verification, while the End-of-Life Vehicles Regulation makes manufacturers cover the cost of collecting and treating EU end-of-life vehicles.
frame_summary: Fastmarkets is arguing that scrap retention is being pulled by procurement contracts and producer-responsibility law from the demand side, not only pushed by trade policy from the supply side.
verbatim_quote: Hydro CIRCAL is recycled aluminium made with at least 75% post-consumer scrap, recovered from end-of-life products including windows, facades, vehicles and consumer electronics. The post-consumer scrap content is tracked and documented for each production batch in a process verified by classification organization DNV.
verbatim_list: The regulation also expands carmakers’ scrap management responsibility, requiring manufacturers to cover the cost of collecting and treating end-of-life vehicles in the EU.
notes: Shows the corporate-side mechanism: provenance-verified scrap becoming a contracted input.

title: Aluminum scrap export duty seen as test case for wider EU export controls
key_claim: The EU intends to use a planned export duty on aluminium scrap as a test case for similar measures on copper, rare-earth magnets and batteries, with a tariff possibly revealed on 9 September alongside a proposal on addressing supply chain dependencies.
frame_summary: E&E News is arguing that the aluminium measure is a template rather than a one-off, which is what makes it a doctrine rather than a sectoral fix.
verbatim_quote: BRUSSELS — The EU intends to use a planned export duty on aluminum scrap as a test case for similar measures on copper, rare-earth magnets and batteries.
notes: Load-bearing for the generalisation claim; the only source that states the test-case intention directly.

title: EU aluminium scrap export curbs delayed until September, group and sources say
key_claim: EU aluminium scrap exports hit a record 1.27-million tonnes in 2025, up about 50% on 2019 levels, with most going to Asia and the largest volume to India; recyclers counter that only 20% of scrap is exported and much of it is lower grade that cannot be handled in the EU.
frame_summary: Mining Weekly is reporting both the volume case for retention and the recyclers' rebuttal that the retained material would not be usable, which is the substantive dispute inside the policy.
verbatim_quote: European Aluminium, representing producers who favour the export ban, said EU aluminium scrap exports hit a record 1.27-million metric tons in 2025, up about 50% from 2019 levels, with most heading to Asia and the highest amount to India.
verbatim_list: The group says that only 20% of scrap is actually exported and much of this is of a lower grade that cannot be handled in the EU.
notes: Reuters wire copy carried by Creamer Media. Carries both the volume anchor and the counter-case.

title: Offener Brief an EU-Kommission: keine Handelsbeschraenkungen fuer Recycling-Aluminium
key_claim: A coalition of European recycling associations and companies including bvse and BDSV, coordinated by Recycling Europe, formally asked the Commission in an open letter dated 28 May 2026 to reconsider possible export restrictions on aluminium scrap.
frame_summary: The European recycling industry is arguing that retention would damage the circular economy and Europe's industrial base rather than secure it, which is the organised domestic opposition to the measure.
verbatim_quote: In einem gemeinsamen offenen Brief an Exekutivvizepräsident Stéphane Séjourné und Kommissar Maroš Šefčovič hat eine Koalition europäischer Recyclingverbände und -unternehmen - darunter der bvse und die BDSV - die Europäische Kommission aufgefordert, mögliche Exportbeschränkungen für Aluminium-Schrott zu überdenken.
notes: German-language primary trade coverage of the industry counter-position; satisfies the multi-language sourcing rule for an EU-anchored topic.
